title: Commute Cost Calculator: Driving, Parking & Time
description: Calculate monthly and annual commuting costs, including mileage, parking, tolls and time. Compare driving to work with a hybrid or remote schedule.

inputs.name: oneWayDistance
inputs.label: One-way Distance (miles; or km with a per-km cost)

inputs.name: costPerUnitDistance
inputs.label: Vehicle Cost per Mile (or per km)
inputs.presetLabel: Use a reference rate (or enter your own cost below)

inputs.name: parkingAndTollsPerDay
inputs.label: Parking and Tolls per Commute Day (round trip)

inputs.name: hourlyValue
inputs.label: Value of One Hour of Your Time

resultCta.label: Compare office, hybrid and remote schedules
resultCta.note: Use vehicle costs and time separately in the schedule comparison to avoid counting time twice.

methodSummary: Annual commute days = days per week × weeks per year.
Annual vehicle cost = one-way distance × 2 × annual commute days × cost per mile (or km).
Parking and tolls = daily round-trip parking and tolls × annual commute days.
Annual time value = one-way minutes × 2 ÷ 60 × annual commute days × hourly time value.
assumptions: Enter miles with a per-mile rate, or kilometers with a per-kilometer rate; do not mix them. US IRS presets are in USD per mile.
Vehicle costs include fuel, maintenance and depreciation when your chosen per-mile rate includes them. Do not add those costs again.
The schedule is constant. Use your actual commuting weeks after leave and holidays; do not assume 52 weeks if you take time off.
insights: At 30 minutes each way, five days a week and 48 weeks a year, you spend 240 hours commuting.
Reducing office days from five to three cuts modeled mileage, parking, tolls and commute hours by 40%; fixed vehicle ownership costs may remain.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my monthly commute cost?
faqs.a: Multiply round-trip distance by cost per mile, add daily parking and tolls, then multiply by commute days per week and weeks per year. Divide by 12. This is an annualized monthly average.

faqs.q: Does this calculate gas costs or total vehicle costs?
faqs.a: It uses the per-mile or per-kilometer amount you enter. For gas only, divide price per gallon by miles per gallon. For a broader estimate, include maintenance and depreciation in that rate. Do not count gas twice.

faqs.q: Can I use the IRS mileage rate for commuting?
faqs.a: You can use it as a reference for vehicle cost, but it is a business mileage rate, not a commuting deduction. The 2026 rate is 72.5 cents per mile for January–June and 76 cents per mile for July–December. Choose the period you are modeling or enter a mileage-weighted rate.

faqs.q: How do I include parking and tolls?
faqs.a: Enter the total you pay for a full commute day in Parking and Tolls. For a fixed monthly parking pass, convert its annual cost to a daily amount using your annual commute days; a fixed pass may not get cheaper with fewer office days.

faqs.q: What is my commute time worth?
faqs.a: Enter the amount you would personally pay to recover an hour. Try zero, half your hourly pay, and your hourly pay to see the range. This is subjective value, not guaranteed additional income.

faqs.q: Can I compare a hybrid schedule?
faqs.a: Change days commuting per week to two or three and compare with five. The linked office, hybrid and remote calculator compares all three schedules together.

faqs.q: Can I use this for public transportation?
faqs.a: This tool is designed for distance-based driving costs. Use the office, hybrid and remote calculator for a daily transit cost; spread the annual price of a fixed pass across the days you actually commute.

useCases: Deciding between two job offers with different locations.
Evaluating the true value of a Remote vs. Hybrid role.
Calculating potential savings from moving house.
richContent:
How much does a 30-mile round trip cost?

This example uses 15 miles and 30 minutes each way, 48 commuting weeks, a chosen vehicle cost of $0.50 per mile, $5 daily parking and tolls, and time valued at $25 per hour. The vehicle rate is an illustrative assumption, not a national average.

ScheduleVehicle + parking / yearHours / yearCost including time
5 office days / week$4,800240$10,800
3 office days / week$2,880144$6,480
2 office days / week$1,92096$4,320

Is the commute worth the higher salary?

Compare the additional take-home pay with the additional cash costs first. Then decide whether the remaining gain compensates you for the travel time. A $10,000 gross raise is not $10,000 of spendable income, and $6,000 of time value is not a cash expense.

Use the job offer comparison calculator for salary and benefits, then the office, hybrid and remote calculator for working patterns.
quickAnswer: A 15-mile, 30-minute one-way drive, five days a week for 48 weeks, adds up to 7,200 miles and 240 hours a year. Vehicle costs and the value of your time are shown separately.
resultNote: Time value is an opportunity cost, not a bill or extra salary. A per-mile vehicle estimate may include fixed costs you would still pay when working remotely. Ordinary commuting is generally not tax-deductible.
